doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Trios, electric questions and the big band
title: Electric piano and Avery Sharpe's electric bass
summary: Tyner explains he used a Kurzweil only with headphones, accepted Avery's electric bass, and praises Avery as a person.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And also Avery was playing electric bass. Now I don’t have any recollection or any documentation of you playing any electrical instruments. Not expanding into even electric piano let alone synthesizer or any of that. So that seemed to be something that didn’t interest you.
Yeah well I had an electric piano but it was only so I could . . .
Put earphones on.
Yeah, use earphones with it. I could play at night and nobody would hear anything if I used earphones. If I had to write some music for a recording session and I didn’t have enough
time during the daytime, I couldn’t do it because of where I was situated . . . those headphones have helped a lot.
What type of electric piano was it? Was it a Fender Rhodes or Hohner?
Kurzweil.
Kurzweil. Yeah that’s right. Good memory.
OK. Avery is now using electric bass in your group so was that something that you accepted or was that something that you said, “Oh.” How did that come about?
Well see when I turned up and saw dancing and he’s playing electric . . . it works good. Tell Aaron to do the backbeat, that worked well! The back beat and electric guitar (laughs).
Avery put out a CD either last year or the year before called Legends and Mentors. Did you hear that one?
Yeah.
Yeah with Yusef (Lateef), him and Archie Shepp. Yeah because he mailed one to us, but you want to find about the electric, go ahead.
Yeah, I guess that was OK, that was something that you either you accepted or encourage.
And I had an electric piano in my mother's shop, beauty shop.
Was that electric?
Electric.
No, it was a small acoustic.
Maybe it wasn’t. Oh that’s right.
It was a small acoustic, the Spinet.
Like a Spinet.
I thought I had, didn’t I have an electric and an upright? I’m trying to think of where the electric came in.
He was saying why Avery played electric bass and you never used an electric piano.
Yeah, well the only time I used an electric piano was in Ma’s beauty shop. I mean sometimes I would have a rehearsal-
Because you always had an acoustic, Steinway. Maybe in your apartment in New York?
Yeah I know I had a Steinway, but I mean . . .
Maybe in your apartment in New York.
Yeah I thought I had one in my apartment.
So Avery served a long tenure with you.
Twenty something years.
Yeah over twenty years, nice sympatico with him. We were talking off mic earlier, there is always a personal connection, not just a musical connection.
He’s a nice guy too.
Beautiful person.
Yeah, beautiful person, real nice, respectful, and he was very serious about what he was doing.
